subject.title: Codex-OAuth models fail over incorrectly — sibling model with healthy per-model quota still drops to non-codex fallback

question: For Codex OAuth sibling-model failover, should OpenClaw keep Codex models on the app-server and investigate the suspected upstream websocket/rate-limit behavior, or add a supported direct-runtime Codex Harmony adapter/fallback?
rationale: The choice changes runtime ownership, provider routing, and tool-call parsing behavior, and source inspection cannot replace live Codex quota proof for the app-server 429.

options.title: Investigate app-server first
options.body: Keep the Codex app-server as the default, finish #99810, and require live proof of the suspected upstream websocket/rate-limit context bug before changing routing.

options.title: Add direct Harmony adapter
options.body: Implement and prove Codex Harmony tool-call parsing in the direct Responses runtime before considering a direct-runtime fallback for Codex OAuth models.

options.title: Wait for stronger repro
options.body: Leave the issue open for redacted logs or maintainer-owned live repro before choosing either runtime direction.

recommendation.title: Investigate app-server first
recommendation.body: Keep the Codex app-server as the default, finish #99810, and require live proof of the suspected upstream websocket/rate-limit context bug before changing routing.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent Codex app-server and OpenAI/Codex routing work is closest to the runtime-direction decision.
